assembly_notes:
DELIBERATE DOMAIN REDUCTION (recorded, not silent). core_domain was 6 x 5 x 4 x 4 x 4 x 3 = 5760 with two multiplicities; it is now 6 x 5 x 4 x 4 x 4 = 1920 with ONE multiplicity. `guide_roller` is no longer an independent slot - the roller form is derived from `bender_topology` - and `guide_roller_count` is no longer a multiplicity - the station count is derived from `former_count` and the host's placement law. WHY IT WAS DONE: preflight probe cost. 26 candidates plus 14 candidate x N min/max pairs is about 40 builds against a 120 s soft semantic budget and a 12 s per-build cap, and this category's builds run 2.5-3 s each. WHAT WAS GIVEN UP: 3840 core combinations - every pairing of a roller form with a host that form is not attested on - plus roller counts that differ from the former count, and any roller count above 4 (the source's five-station rack is now reachable only at former_count 4). WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SAYS, stated because the record must be accurate: guide rollers are NOT an L5-only feature. They are attested on L1 (004, guide_roller_0/1 on the rail), L2 (005, one roller on the cradle) and L5 (two and three stations), with two independently measured placement laws. What IS true, and what justifies this particular mapping, is that each roller FORM appears on exactly one lineage and never travels to a foreign host, and that L3 and L4 carry no frame-borne guide roller at all - so the slot was over-declared. The count reduction is budget rather than evidence, and is marked as such. Both measured laws stay written down verbatim in binding roller_track_to_guide_rollers so the cut is reversible.

IDENTITY. A grounded or bench/vise-mounted forming tool whose defining articulation is a grooved former and a long moving member sweeping about a shared +Z bend axis, plus one or more spinning guide rollers and at least one adjustment degree of freedom. +Z is the bend axis in every seed; +X is the pipe feed direction; z=0 is the mount's ground plane. Fifteen of the twenty source records use ONLY (0,0,1) joints; the exceptions are the ram_tripod pump handle (0,1,0), the cast bench adjustment screw (1,0,0) and the two prismatic ram axes.

DOMAIN. core_domain = 6 bender_topology x 5 drive x 4 former_profile x 4 follower_module x 4 mount x 3 guide_roller = 5760 combinations, every one of which must build - TemplateDomain has no compatibility gates. raw_domain = 5760 x 4 former_count values x 5 guide_roller_count values = 115200. Palette, handle length, former size class, mount height and index-plate hole density are continuous or decorative and count toward neither.

STRUCTURAL-FAMILY CALL. The six bender_topology candidates are ONE family, not six slots. Three of them are whole hosts drawn from three unrelated code lineages (different root part, 4/6/8 parts, 3/5/7 joints, revolute vs prismatic primary motion, scale 0.33 m to 1.11 m, 1130-1490 changed lines pairwise); the other three are host-local but host-specific. Declaring them independent would force combinations the pool never builds, such as a 0.050 m crescent shoe on a 0.029 m plier former. The contrast that proves the boundary is mount: mount_vise_mounted_frame changes NOTHING above the spindle, only SPINDLE_Z 0.936 -> 0.336 plus a new base, so mount IS an independent slot.

CROSS-SLOT RISKS, resolved by derivation and never by a gate:
(a) screw_feed_ram converts the primary joint REVOLUTE -> PRISMATIC. Only ram_tripod publishes a native ram_axis, so on the other five hosts binding ram_axis_to_crank_link instantiates an authored ram_crank_link part plus one revolute joint, with crank_link_length_m sized so the full ram stroke maps onto the host's full sweep. Named corner: screw_ram_on_rotary_host (five combinations).
(b) hand_lever_plier has no base at all, so every mount candidate derives a clamp collar around its lower tang. Named corner: mount_on_hand_tool (four combinations).
(c) former_count uses three different placement laws and guide_roller_count two; which law applies is a DERIVED value (former_placement_law, guide_placement_law), not a comment, so a rail-head host indexes formers along +X while a single-pivot host indexes them on a circle. Named corners: angular_turret_max_n, linear_rack_max_n, pipe_path_rollers_max_n.
(d) rotary_draw_wrap_wheel wraps 300 degrees and needs its mouth to face the follower; crescent_conduit_shoe wraps the former from outside. Both derive from former_outer_r_m, so the largest-profile-on-smallest-host combination is a corner rather than an exclusion: named corner wrap_wheel_on_hand_tool.

ALLOWANCES. Every one of the 20 source records calls ctx.allow_overlap - about 70 sites in total - and preflight BLOCKS allow_overlap for Design-backed templates. ctx.allow_isolated_part is NOT blocked and is the sanctioned escape for a member carried by its joint on a running clearance; the pool already uses it three times for the loose spare die. Nine causes and their fixes:
1. Bore equal to or smaller than the shaft (18 sites) -> binding shaft_to_bore_clearance, bore = shaft + 0.03*shaft + 0.0002, plus allow_isolated_part. LINEAGE L3 BORES EVERY HOLE 0.5-1.0 mm UNDER ITS PIN (hub 0.010 vs spindle 0.011, arm 0.0055 vs pin 0.006, bracket 0.0065 vs axle 0.007) and pedestal_ladder_rail bores its die at exactly the pin radius; the rebuild inverts the sign. This is a stated correction, not a silent one.
2. Exactly-tangent seats, distance zero (26 sites) -> merge FIXED children such as the pipe cradle into the frame part (intra-part embedding is free per MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c), and offset moving seats by 0.2 mm.
3. Pawl buried in the ratchet (2 sites) -> pawl tip at tooth_tip_r + 0.0003 on a flank.
4. Shoe ring fouling the lever boss (1 site) -> bore the boss full height at ring OD + 1 mm instead of cutting a rectangular slot.
5. Roller declared overlapping a shoe bore it already clears (1 site) -> drop the allowance, keep expect_within.
6. Chain wrapping sprockets that live on a different part (5 sites) -> the chain becomes its own part with band inner radius = tip radius + 0.0003 and allow_isolated_part.
7. Turret former against its own bearing (3 sites) -> derive bearing top from the seat.
8. Workpiece against the former and every roller (12 sites) -> DROP the workpiece part; both origins explicitly omit the loose demonstration tube.
9. Prismatic stop stem inside a solid frame (3 sites) -> cut a real bore per MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 7.

VISUAL AND COLLISION BUDGET. sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py:94-118 derives one collision solid per visual, 1:1. Source seeds emit 31-38 visuals; the worst cases are 16 chain_pin cylinders embedded in the chain band, 8 grip ribs on a handle, 5 primitives per guide roller and 4 rigid caster wheels. Four deliberate deviations, each stated rather than silently applied: (i) guide rollers are welded into one CAD solid using the route cast_bench_mimic already takes, saving 4*N collision solids; (ii) grip ribs and chain pins are unioned into their host solid, saving 23 more; (iii) the workpiece is dropped; (iv) casters become REAL parts. Target budget is under 20 collision solids per seed at N=1.

CASTER DEVIATION IN FULL. MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 5 requires a caster to have a vertical swivel axis and a spin axis through the wheel centre. The source gives it neither: four rigid wheel visuals on `stand`, no joints, and a 0.056-wide wheel inside a fork whose inner faces are 0.026 apart - legal only while wheel and fork are visuals of the same part. The rebuild adds 4 caster_swivel parts and 4 caster_wheel parts with 4 REVOLUTE (0,0,1) and 4 CONTINUOUS local-X joints, widens the fork to wheel width + 2 x fork_side_clearance_m, and re-grounds the deck so the contact patch is z=0 rather than the source's z=-0.108. That is 8 new parts and 8 new joints relative to the source, and it is the largest deviation in this design.

MULTIPLICITY. former_count in {1,2,3,4}: N=1 is both origins and twelve variants, N=2 and N=3 are source-attested, and N=4 is an extrapolation the angular law's own clearance condition already covers - 2R*sin(pi/4) = 0.1414 against 2*0.035 + 0.006 = 0.076 at the source's R = 0.100. N=5 is deliberately NOT declared for formers: the pool's 'five' counts roller stations, not formers. guide_roller_count in {1,2,3,4,5} with every endpoint source-attested - 1 from cast_bench_mimic, 2 from pedestal_ladder_rail, 3 from guide_roller_count_3, 5 from the five-station rack, whose host derivation (rack_length = (x_{N-1} - PIVOT_X) + 0.145, base plate 0.40 -> 0.76, cradle relocated) is fully index-general.

ANCHOR SCOPING.
- pipe_bender_rotating_former: SCOPED DELIBERATELY: pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle is excluded because its former is a FIXED feature of the root part (Cylinder visuals on `stand`, L198-L209) and the handle is what sweeps. That is source-attested per candidate, not a modelling shortcut, so the anchor is scoped rather than weakened for everyone.
- pipe_bender_drive_on_primary_axis: The revolute relation holds for four of the five drives. screw_feed_ram contributes a PRISMATIC joint (L356-L369); on ram_tripod it replaces the primary joint outright and on the other five hosts the authored ram_crank_link restores the revolute relation between bender_frame and moving_member, so the anchor is satisfied through the link rather than directly. That is what binding ram_axis_to_crank_link exists to guarantee.

PART TREE. mount_base (root) -> bender_frame -> {N formers in parallel, moving_member, N guide rollers} and moving_member -> follower. drive_member parents to the frame for every candidate. Seeds carry 5 + former_count + guide_roller_count parts at minimum, plus 8 for caster_deck and 1 for the screw ram's crank link.

ONE CAUTION THE POOL CANNOT ANSWER. Source author tests are far weaker than the template checks - every record leans on allow_overlap and fail_if_parts_overlap_in_sampled_poses never ran against them. A construction being source-attested does not mean it survives QC; the bore-clearance evidence above is exactly that case.

derived.name: bore_clearance_m
derived.rationale: THE central fit rule of the category, measured across the whole pool and fitted to three independent records at once: cast_bench_mimic 0.0015 at shaft 0.0090 (L82 vs L185), ram_tripod 0.0009 at shaft 0.0075 (L73 vs L465), hand_lever_plier 0.0003 at shaft 0.0052 (L347 vs L250). CORRECTION APPLIED, stated rather than silent: lineage L3 (pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle and everything forked from it) bores every hole 0.5-1.0 mm UNDER its pin - hub bore 0.010 vs spindle 0.011, arm bore 0.0055 vs pin 0.006, bracket bore 0.0065 vs axle 0.007 - and pedestal_ladder_rail bores its die at exactly the pin radius (0.010 vs 0.010). Those are the sole cause of 18 of the pool's ~70 allow_overlap sites. The rebuild inverts the sign.

derived.name: former_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: Through bore of every former, cut for real so the pin passes without a solid intersection. The clearance is geometric, not an allowance.

derived.name: guide_roller_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: Same rule on the roller axles. Source cast_bench_mimic bores the guide roller at 0.0040 against a 0.0040 pin (L318 vs L304) - exact equality, hence its allow_overlap at L608-L617; ram_tripod does it correctly at 0.0084 against 0.0075.

derived.name: guide_roller_axle_r_m
derived.rationale: Roller axles are consistently about half the main spindle: 0.0075 vs 0.0110 (ram_tripod L425 vs pedestal L193), 0.0040 vs 0.0090 (cast_bench_mimic L304 vs L185), 0.0034 vs 0.0046 (hand_lever_plier L319 vs L244).

derived.name: drive_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: The drive member's hub bore. hand_lever_plier authors NO bore at all in its handle cheek (circle(0.023) solid over a 0.0046 pin, L285 vs L244), which is why it needs allow_overlap at L608-L614; the rebuild cuts one.

derived.name: moving_member_support
derived.rationale: Members carried by their joint on a running clearance are declared with ctx.allow_isolated_part, which preflight explicitly does NOT block. Closing the clearance to satisfy fail_if_isolated_parts would re-create the interference the pool already suffers from.

derived.name: thrust_washer_height_m
derived.rationale: Thrust washer / bearing puck under the former. Source cast_bench_mimic L66-L68: _cylinder_z(0.025, 0.004, z0=0.016) minus a 0.0105 bore, i.e. 0.004 on a 0.064 former; ram_tripod L458-L462 uses a 0.010 puck on a 0.064 former.

derived.name: former_running_gap_m
derived.rationale: AUDIT CORRECTION (MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c, rewritten). The former used to be seated EXACTLY on the thrust-washer top, reproducing cast_bench_mimic's expect_contact(contact_tol=0.0005) at L573-L580. Exact part-to-part tangency is now declared fragile, and this particular contact is between a REVOLUTE member and its host, so the honest fix is not an overlap but an explicit running clearance: the former is carried by its joint and declared with ctx.allow_isolated_part, exactly as binding shaft_to_bore_clearance already states for every other bore. 0.2 mm is the same offset the rebuild uses under the guide rollers (roller_seat_z_m) and the turret bearings (turret_bearing_top_z_m), so all three rotating seats now share one number.

derived.name: former_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: THE seat derivation. cast_bench_mimic L66-L68 puts the washer top at z 0.020 and then authors base_to_die at exactly (0,0,0.020) (L378) with expect_contact(contact_tol=0.0005) (L573-L580). ram_tripod does the same with a bearing puck whose top is 0.3175 and a former extruded +-0.0225 about a joint at 0.340. The seat plane is READ OFF the washer, never authored twice. former_count_3 breaks the rule - its turret bearing top is 0.332 against a former underside at 0.3175, 14.5 mm of interference and one more allow_overlap (L888-L898) - and the rebuild re-derives it.

derived.name: moving_member_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: The lever/handle rides above the former. cast_bench_mimic: former top 0.020 + 0.035 = 0.055 and base_to_lever sits at 0.056 (L362), a 1 mm gap.

derived.name: lever_seat_gap_m
derived.rationale: Running gap between the former's top face and the moving member above it, from cast_bench_mimic L362 vs L378 + L73-L75.

derived.name: primary_axis_z_m
derived.rationale: Where the primary revolute actually lives. On five hosts it is the former's own axis; on pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle the former is a fixed feature of the root part (L198-L203) and the primary joint belongs to the handle, so the axis datum shifts.

derived.expression: head_height_m if bender_topology == 'pedestal_ladder_rail' else (head_plate_stack_m if bender_topology == 'pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle' else cheek_height_m)
derived.name: host_stack_z_m
derived.rationale: Height the host itself adds between the mount deck and the former seat. 0.583 for the ladder-rail head (L21), 0.122 for the stacked-plate head, 0.008 for the cast bench plate, 0.0 for the hand tool.

derived.expression: handle_length_m if drive == 'lever_handle' else (wheel_outer_r_m if drive == 'geared_handwheel' else (driven_pitch_r_m if drive == 'chain_sprocket_drive' else (sector_outer_r_m if drive == 'ratchet_sector_drive' else screw_handwheel_r_m)))
derived.name: drive_torque_radius_m
derived.rationale: One number the host can size its clearance envelope against, whichever drive is fitted. Also the reason effort tracks the drive and not just scale: 140-420 for levers, 900-1200 for the mimicked bench die, 9000 for the screw, 18000 for the hydraulic ram.

derived.name: gear_tip_r_driver_m
derived.rationale: Tip radius of the driving toothed member. _sprocket L105-L144 derives tip = 0.94*pr + 0.5*0.34*pr = 1.11*pr; the spur route adds the tooth depth to the base radius (hand_lever_plier L146-L155).

derived.name: gear_tip_r_driven_m
derived.rationale: Tip radius of the driven member on the primary axis. hand_lever_plier L255-L264 puts a 22-tooth ring of base radius 0.0293 on a 0.029 former, i.e. roughly the former radius.

derived.name: gear_centre_distance_m
derived.rationale: THE mesh rule, measured not guessed. hand_lever_plier is the pool's only real gear pair and it is built TANGENT: tips 0.0313 and 0.0158, centres (0.067, 0.007) and (0.024, -0.013) -> 0.04742 against a tip sum of 0.0471, a 0.32 mm gap, asserted as a mesh with expect_contact(contact_tol=0.0008) at L592-L599. Teeth NEVER overlap; MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 4 forbids substituting bulk overlap for mesh.

derived.name: gear_axial_overlap_m
derived.rationale: Axial engagement of the two toothed rings. hand_lever_plier: frame ring z 0.020..0.024 against a roller gear at 0.017..0.021 after its joint origin (L255-L264, L146-L155, L388).

derived.name: sprocket_root_r_m
derived.rationale: _sprocket L114: root_radius = pitch_radius * 0.82.

derived.name: sprocket_tooth_width_m
derived.rationale: _sprocket L120: tangential width is 48 percent of the pitch, floored at 0.0022. The spur equivalent is 58 percent (_toothed_disk L108) and the hand tool's ring is about 40 percent (0.0030 on a 0.0084 pitch), so the gullet is always real.

derived.name: sprocket_hub_r_m
derived.rationale: _sprocket L131: hub = pitch_radius * 0.42.

derived.name: chain_band_inner_r_m
derived.rationale: The chain wraps on the tip circle plus the same 0.3 mm the gear pair uses. The source instead offsets both runs by the MEAN pitch radius (_chain_loop L160), which leaves it 2 mm off tangency and forces three allow_overlap sites.

derived.name: pawl_tip_r_m
derived.rationale: Pawl tip radius at rest. The sector's own tooth tip is outer + 0.020 (L135); the pawl body must lie wholly OUTSIDE that circle and engage a flank. Both pool examples instead bury the pawl 8.5-8.7 mm inside the tooth circle (L322, and ratcheting_crossbow L233 vs L110), which is allowance group 3.

derived.name: sector_tooth_half_width_m
derived.rationale: The source's own teeth just touch: half-width 0.010 at r 0.162 is 7.07 deg of arc against a 6.909 deg pitch (L127-L140). Capping at 45 percent of the pitch restores a gullet.

derived.name: drive_second_axis_r_m
derived.rationale: Idler / sector pin on the frame for the two drives that need a second station. hand_lever_plier runs a 0.0046 pivot pin against a 0.0052 former axle (L244, L250); the L3 sector pin is 0.006 against an 0.011 spindle (L240, L193).

derived.name: drive_output_z_m
derived.rationale: Z of the drive's own toothed/geared plane above the primary axis datum.

derived.name: drive_stack_offset_m
derived.rationale: hand_lever_plier stacks the ring 0.004 above the former top (L255-L264 z0=0.020 on an 0.018 former seated at 0.002).

derived.name: primary_joint_type
derived.rationale: screw_feed_ram converts the primary joint from REVOLUTE to PRISMATIC (L356-L369, axis (1,0,0), 0..0.090, effort 9000) and deletes the hub capture. Only ram_tripod publishes a native ram_axis (frame_to_ram, L581-L594), so only there does the screw replace the primary joint outright.

derived.name: ram_crank_link_required
derived.rationale: THE cross-slot gate expressed as a derivation instead of a compatibility gate. On the five rotary hosts the screw feed drives an authored `ram_crank_link` part with one extra revolute joint, so a linear feed still produces the rotary sweep. Adding one link part is a local adaptation - it changes neither the host's part tree above the primary axis nor its silhouette - which is what keeps all 30 drive x topology pairs inside the complete-combination principle. Named corner: screw_ram_on_rotary_host.

derived.name: crank_link_length_m
derived.rationale: Crank radius that maps the full ram stroke onto the host's full sweep. The chord of a sweep at radius r is 2*r*sin(sweep/2), so inverting it gives the shortest link that still reaches both stroke ends, floored so the link always clears the former.

derived.name: ram_stroke_to_sweep_rad
derived.rationale: The realised sweep, fed back into the primary joint limits so the ram's lower/upper and the primary joint's lower/upper are the same motion. Motion QC drives both ends.

derived.name: crank_pin_r_m
derived.rationale: Pin joining the ram nut to the crank link; its bore follows shaft_to_bore_clearance like every other bore in the model.

derived.expression: sweep_upper_rad if bender_topology == 'cast_bench_mimic' else (handle_open_rad if bender_topology == 'hand_lever_plier' else 1.10)
derived.name: primary_sweep_rad
derived.rationale: Total primary sweep per host: 2.35 (cast_bench_mimic L368), 2.15 (pedestal_ladder_rail lever_pivot -2.00..0.15, L310-L314), 1.10 (pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle -0.38..0.72, L357), 0.72 (hand_lever_plier -0.14..0.58, L338-L343), 0.70 (ram_tripod -0.35..0.35, L602-L606).

derived.name: ram_axis_z_m
derived.rationale: Height of the ram / screw centre line. ram_tripod runs its ram at z 0.305 against a former joint at 0.340 (L586, L600); the screw drive runs at z 0.183 in the handle frame (L114).

derived.name: ram_shaft_r_m
derived.rationale: Ram / screw core radius published on the ram_axis interface.

derived.name: groove_depth_m
derived.rationale: Groove depth, capped so the die never swallows more than 85 percent of the tube radius. Pool ratios of depth to tube radius: 0.79 (pedestal_ladder_rail, 0.011/0.014), 0.64 (cast_bench_mimic, 0.011/0.0173), 0.31 (rotary_draw_wrap_wheel, 0.004/0.013). multi_radius_stepped states the same intent as a formula: min(R*(0.105-0.015*i), band_h*0.34) at L79.

derived.name: groove_root_r_m
derived.rationale: Radius of the groove floor. Source values: 0.075 on an 0.086 former (pedestal_ladder_rail L72-L76), 0.053 on 0.064 (cast_bench_mimic L73-L75), 0.069 flat floor on 0.086 (square_tube_channel L25), 0.062 on 0.066 (rotary_draw_wrap_wheel L44-L45).

derived.name: bend_radius_m
derived.rationale: The bend the tool actually produces: the tube centreline runs on the groove root circle. ram_tripod builds its workpiece on exactly this radius (0.0769 at L118 against a 0.064 former).

derived.name: groove_height_m
derived.rationale: Axial height of the groove between the flanges. cast_bench_mimic: 0.021 between two 0.007 flanges in a 0.035 former (L73-L75).

derived.expression: flange_height_ratio * former_height_m if former_profile == 'round_flanged_groove' else wrap_flange_height_m
derived.name: former_flange_h_m
derived.rationale: Flange height per profile candidate: 0.007/0.035 (round), 0.0045 in a 0.045 wheel (rotary draw L57-L62), 0.011/0.058 (ladder rail).

derived.name: groove_mid_z_m
derived.rationale: Mid-plane of the groove in the former's own frame; the follower and guide rollers align their tube seats to it.

derived.name: cheek_relief_r_m
derived.rationale: Host relief the frame must cut so the former is wrapped, not pierced. cast_bench_mimic L57 cuts _cylinder_z(0.069, 0.050) around a 0.064 former; three_roll_pyramid re-derives it to 0.043 for a 0.038 former (L58). MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 7: this is the mechanism, not decoration.

derived.name: follower_station_r_m
derived.rationale: Plan radius from the primary axis to the follower's own axis. cast_bench_mimic puts the shoe at (0.065, -0.060) = 0.0885 against a bend radius of 0.053 + 0.0173 = 0.0703 (L395, L73-L75); three_roll_pyramid moves it to (0.080, -0.080) = 0.113 when the rolls grow (L399).

derived.name: follower_station_z_m
derived.rationale: cast_bench_mimic drops the shoe joint 0.012 below the lever frame (L395); pedestal_ladder_rail drops it 0.042 (L322).

derived.name: follower_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: The follower's tube seat must sit on the former's groove mid-plane, or the tube is pinched off-centre.

derived.name: crescent_inner_r_m
derived.rationale: crescent_conduit_shoe only. Source L101-L106: inner 0.050 around the family's 0.040 fixed die = 0.010 running gap.

derived.name: roller_pocket_r_m
derived.rationale: Clearance pocket the crescent cuts for the pressure roller. Source L127-L132: circle(0.024) for a roller of OD 0.019 with a 0.0215 flange, i.e. 2.5 mm.

derived.name: shoe_boss_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: CORRECTION APPLIED: cast_bench_mimic cuts a RECTANGULAR slot (box(0.031, 0.026, 0.050), L109) through a circle(0.030) boss, but the shoe ring is OD 0.0215 - wider than the slot half-width 0.0155 - so the ring fouls the boss and the record declares allow_overlap at L627-L636. The rebuild bores the boss full height at ring OD + 1 mm instead.

derived.expression: 'flanged_barrel_roller' if bender_topology in ('pedestal_ladder_rail', 'pedestal_fixed_die_swing_handle') else ('annular_disc_roller' if bender_topology == 'ram_tripod' else 'bored_spool_roller')
derived.name: guide_roller_form
derived.rationale: DELIBERATE DOMAIN REDUCTION, recorded rather than silent. guide_roller was an independent slot with three candidates; it is now DERIVED from bender_topology, taking core_domain from 5760 to 1920 and preflight probe builds from about 40 to about 26. The REASON for reducing at all is compile and probe budget against a 120 s soft semantic budget. The particular mapping is evidence-backed rather than arbitrary: each roller FORM appears on exactly one lineage and never travels - flanged_barrel_roller is L1 only (004 L200-L233), bored_spool_roller is L2 only (005 L122-L139), annular_disc_roller is L5 only (guide_roller_count_3 L34-L40) - and no record in the pool pairs a roller form with a foreign host. That is the same host-local-but-host-specific test that folded three candidates into bender_topology. Lineages L3 and L4 carry no frame-borne guide roller at all: hickey_style_offset has only `pressure_roller` on the handle (L321-L348) and geared_ring_roller only `follower_roller` (L376-L391), so declaring the slot independent over all six topologies asserted two host families the pool never builds rollers on. NOTE, because the record must be accurate: guide rollers are NOT an L5-only feature - they are attested on L1 (004, two stations), L2 (005, one station on the cradle) and L5 (two and three stations), with TWO measured placement laws. WHAT WAS GIVEN UP: the 3840 core combinations that paired a roller form with a host it is not attested on.

derived.name: guide_roller_count_derived
derived.rationale: DELIBERATE DOMAIN REDUCTION, recorded rather than silent. guide_roller_count was a declared multiplicity over {1,2,3,4,5}; it is now DERIVED from former_count, leaving former_count as the template's only multiplicity. The evidence supports it: a second INDEPENDENT N was never attested. On the L1 family the SAME N drives both station sets - former_count_2 L227-L228 loops the roller stations `x = 0.145 + 0.110*i` over FORMER_COUNT, and former_count_5 L126-L158 / L263-L306 builds five roller + block + screw stations from that same FORMER_COUNT.
